category_title: Dominant preschool children who frequently report peers' norm violations
scenario_title: Reporting breaches of simple social norms without a clear victim
minimal_context: The student is participating in daily classroom activities and observing peers playing with dolls in the preschool classroom.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: It is time for free play. You can play with the dolls over here.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: I get to hand out the dolls because I'm in charge.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Just make sure you are playing.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: Teacher, you need to look at them right now.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: They’re being very loud. And they went into the wrong area of the classroom!

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: It is time for free play. You can play with the dolls over here.

STUDENT: I get to hand out the dolls because I'm in charge.

TUTOR: Just make sure you are playing.

STUDENT: Teacher, you need to look at them right now.

TUTOR: What is it?

STUDENT: They’re being very loud. And they went into the wrong area of the classroom!

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When peers breach simple social norms, such as shouting or going into inappropriate areas of the classroom
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Generalizes the form of communication used for harm to report instances of simple social norm breaches where there is no clear victim
challenging_behavior_trigger.internal_state: Less shy about the specific activity of drawing an adult's attention to social problems

behavior_patterns.condition: When observing a breach of social convention
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Reports the transgression to the teacher to manipulate adult attention
behavior_patterns.internal_state: Using tattling as an interpersonal strategy to achieve social dominance
